newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Strike over pay threatened at Venezuela's CANTV.
newsitem.headline: Strike over pay threatened at Venezuela's CANTV.

text.p: Workers at Venezuelan telephone company CANTV threatened Tuesday to go on strike this week over pay after rejecting a "petty" 20 percent wage increase offer.
The workers' union in the central Federal District (Caracas) and Miranda states, one of the largest at CANTV, called for a general assembly Wednesday afternoon to take a strike vote.
"The petty offers of a 20 percent wage increase have infuriated all (CANTV) workers," the union said in a statement.
CANTV, which debuted on world stock markets in November with a $1 billion share offer, employs about 17,000 people. It increased its rates an average 20 percent from January 1.

The union statement said, "Workers fail to understand why a company that had profits of about 100 billion bolivars and pays top executives such as (President) Gustavo Roosen salaries over 11 million bolivars a month ($23,000) refused to grant workers a fair collective contract."
